econ.money.title: External API · spend in money
econ.money.empty: Appears the same way tokens do (AGENTS.md §3): a node called through an external model directly (Bash, not the Agent tool) writes a history line with $. Until there is such a line the section waits for the first one — it is not removed or hidden.
econ.money.note: Format — AGENTS.md §3: $X.XXXXXX (provider/model) in the same attempt line as the tokens. The numbers come from the bridge response (.claude/scripts/external-model-bridge.cjs), not estimated by eye.
econ.l1.perCardNone: no closed cards with a recorded spend yet
econ.trend.empty: No dated attempts — the chart appears after the first record.
econ.trend.aria: Tokens per day and tokens per card
econ.trend.line: Line: tokens per closed card by closing date, the goal is down.
econ.trend.noLine: No line: there are no closed cards on these dates yet.
econ.weeks.few: fewer than two weeks with work so far — the trend is not visible yet.
econ.weeks.up: rising: from {a} ({wa}) to {b} ({wb}) — more re-reads per work token.
econ.l2.noInstr: The instruction share was not measured — cache-read is not recorded in any attempt.
econ.l2.onlyCC: counted for claude-code only — pick that tag above
econ.top.title: Most expensive
econ.top.hint: Look here for what to optimise: many attempts on one card usually mean the slicing was coarse, not that the node worked badly.
econ.routes.title: By route
econ.routes.empty: The by-route breakdown is not built.
econ.routes.hint: Labels route-N, over-N, seg-N, wave-N. Preparation — the share of Spec + Kit in the route tokens; on route-4 Kit is the executor, so preparation is Spec only. Returns — executor attempts beyond the first. Lines marked unknown go to a separate column, not zero.
econ.th.label: Label
econ.blind.none: No blind spots: every card where work happened has a spend record.
econ.blind.title: Blind spots — {cards}
econ.blind.hint: Work happened, spend is not recorded. This is the gap between “done” and “counted”: while it stays, any comparison between nodes is a guess.
econ.days.title: By day
econ.days.hint: Height — tokens per day. Hover to see the numbers.
econ.svc.title: External services
econ.svc.empty: No call recorded yet. A service is Magnific, Aura and the like: they charge in their own unit (credits, minutes), not in tokens or dollars, and are therefore counted separately. Record: a segment N unit (service/operation) in the attempt line, the number from the call response itself, not from a price list. Which services are connected and where their number is read — PROJECT.md, “External services”.
econ.svc.hint: Service units differ and are not summed — they are different facts. Inside a service the spend is split by operation: the price of the same work changes with the mode (for Magnific tripo-image-to-3d costs 580 credits, -high — 1160).
econ.malformed.none: Every line that claims to be an attempt passed parsing.
econ.malformed.title: Spend records that failed parsing — {n}
econ.malformed.hint: The line contains DATE: attempt, — it claims to be a spend record, but does not fit the §3 format and is not counted. This is not the same as a legitimate zero for Intent: there is no spend by law, here it existed and was lost. Most often the problem is not the numbers but the node label — the format expects `Node`, at the very start, while the line starts with an explanation (“`Kit` extraction role (subagent 1/4)”), and the number after it can no longer be read.
econ.weight.unknown: Instruction weight unknown — there is no engine adapter or it did not declare the field.
econ.weight.title: Instruction weight
econ.weight.hint: The law enters the call not once per attempt but anew on every internal step. So shortening the law text is a linear gain, and cutting the number of steps is a multiplicative one. The common part, the same for all nodes: AGENTS.md + .claude/rules/claude-8.md — {tokens} tokens; the rest is added by the role file.
econ.weight.foot: Steps = cache-read ÷ step weight, so the column is empty until R is recorded. Tokens here are counted by the “bytes per token” heuristic, there is no tokenizer. The engine system prompt and tool descriptions are not included — we do not write them, so the real step weight is larger than shown, and the steps fewer.
econ.sess.liveTitle: The file is still being written
econ.sess.none: The ledger is not built. It is counted separately because walking the transcripts takes seconds and gigabytes: node .claude/scripts/session-economy.cjs, then rebuild the dashboard. This is not zero, it is a missing measurement.
econ.sess.hint: Counted from the engine transcripts — every call is recorded there, not only the ones a node remembered to log. Ledger built {age}.
econ.sess.liveCount: Live sessions: {n} — their numbers are incomplete by definition.
econ.sess.money: money is exact for {exact} of {total} sessions, the rest are tariff estimates; together ≈ ${usd}
econ.sw.bar: {week}: {ratio} re-read tokens per output token, {n} sessions
econ.sw.up: Rising: from {a} ({wa}) to {b} ({wb}) — more re-reads per work token, not fewer.
econ.sw.few: Fewer than two weeks with work so far — the trend is not visible yet.
econ.sw.lead: Trend by week (re-reads per work token).
econ.verify.hint: The count rests on deduplication by requestId: without it the sum is inflated tenfold, and plausibility does not show it. So the method is checked against someone else’s books — the cost-state record the engine itself keeps — and the discrepancy is printed always, not only when it matched. More than {pct}% is flagged as suspicious. It can be checked for {checked} of {total} sessions: the others have no such record, and that is shown too, not smoothed over.
econ.verify.note: “Inherited” — calls older than the engine’s reference point: continuing a session after compaction copies the earlier history together with its requestId. They are excluded from the check, otherwise the method would blame the engine for an undercount where the reference boundaries merely differ.
econ.verify.none: No session has a cost-state record — there is nothing to check the method against. The numbers above remain unverified.
econ.codex.none: The measured Codex ledger has not been built yet.
econ.codex.title: Codex: measured spend
econ.codex.hint: Intent ↔ human is counted separately from cards; subagents reach a card only after an explicit binding by id. Transcripts: {n}.
econ.notFor: Not applicable to “{engine}”: these are transcripts of the {owner} engine — pick its tag above.
econ.eng.title: Economy by engine
econ.eng.hint: One column per engine tag from the spend lines; lines without a tag get their own “untagged” column. Tokens of different engines are not added — the “common” column holds only common fields. “Unknown” — lines marked unknown, as a number, not zero.
econ.engineNote: everything that shows tokens is shown for this tag.
bort.inherits: There is no tools field in the frontmatter — the role inherits the whole session set. There is nothing to subtract from, and this is not “zero tools”: it is the maximum.
bort.addrNoOff: Edit address: .claude/agents/{file}, field tools. There is deliberately no “disable” button here — the arsenal is edited by a card through Kit.
bort.ambiguous: the log stores only the tool name, without arguments: which of the Bash(...) entries fired cannot be seen from here
bort.notInLog: there is not a single line for this node in the log — nothing to base a verdict on
bort.undeclared: Pulled in but not declared in the frontmatter (implicit engine tools): {list}. Not included in the weight or the verdicts — this is not our arsenal, there is nothing to trim.
bort.noSource: The node tier cannot be built. The module .claude/scripts/tool-usage.cjs is not found nearby — the dashboard and the protocol are installed by different plugin templates. This is not “no tools”, it is no source.
bort.log.none: There is no log at all. The file .forma/dashboard/tool-usage.log is created by the hook .claude/hooks/tool-usage.sh on its very first call — its absence means the hook has not run once. While there is no log, the verdict on EVERY tool is {unknown}, and none will be called redundant.
bort.log.empty: The log exists, no records. The hook is alive (it wrote the header), there have been no calls since it appeared. The verdict on the whole arsenal is {unknown}.
bort.cov.title: Log coverage: {nodes} of {total}
bort.cov.hint: The log closes exactly one side tightly: no attempts — the tool is wasted. The reverse is wrong twice over. An attempt is written by the hook before the access decision, so it means “was pulled in”, not “worked”. And, more important for trimming: no log for a node does not mean its tools are redundant.
bort.cov.missing: Today the log knows nothing about {names} — their arsenals are marked “unknown”, not “redundant”. A screen that passed them off as dead would suggest cutting what is needed and would look convincing doing it.
bort.cov.total: declared in total {n}, weight ≈ {w} tokens per step (of which proven wasted ≈ {dead})
bort.log.errors: The hook broke on {calls}: those attempts did not make it into the count, and “not used” cannot be read from them. Diagnosis — node .claude/scripts/tool-usage.cjs.
bort.mcp.broken: The file {file} was not parsed — this is a configuration breakage, not “no servers”.
bort.mcp.notFound: not found in the configuration files
bort.mcp.title: Declared in configuration files — {n}
bort.mcp.hint: Two levels: project (.mcp.json, .claude/.mcp.json) travels with the repository, user (~/.claude.json, key mcpServers) — with the person. Each server says where it came from: trimming here affects the whole board, and the named file is the one to edit, not any file.
bort.mcp.noneDeclared: None of the scanned configuration files declares servers.
bort.mcp.incomplete: This list is incomplete by design, not because it is empty. {n} are visible from disk — as many as the files declare. On top of them the session carries account-level connectors (Magnific, Miro, Google Drive, Claude Docs and others connected in claude.ai) and plugin servers: neither is in any local file, and the dashboard cannot read them. This is not “they are absent” — it is “not visible from here”: look in the claude.ai settings (connectors) and in claude plugin list (plugins). The same rule as the “unknown” verdict in the node tier: missing information is passed off neither as empty nor as complete.
bort.ref.title: What the roles refer to
bort.ref.hint: The server name is taken from mcp__<server>__<tool> in the frontmatter. “Not found in the project configuration” is not “not authorised”: a server may arrive as an account connector or a plugin, and they are not visible from here. The third value is here for the same reason as in the verdict above: the screen has no right to call missing information a missing server.
bort.fl.notMeasured: The floor has not been measured yet. Counted by node .forma/dashboard/floor.cjs — walking the transcripts takes seconds and gigabytes, so it does not run on every dashboard build. This is “not measured”, not “zero”.
bort.fl.newProject: On a new project this is the normal state: the first call creates the first transcript, and the line appears by itself.
bort.fl.stats: Measurements: {days} · lowest {min}, highest {max} · from the first measurement to the last the floor {drift}.
bort.fl.reading: Read the slope, not the magnitude. Over two months five roles, fourteen skills, sixty memory entries and an experience graph arrived in the project — and the floor moved by a few thousand and came back. So it is almost entirely not ours, and there is nothing to trim in it: it is the engine’s own prompt. The line is there to catch the day someone connects a server with two hundred tools — and to catch it the next day, not a quarter later on the bill.
bort.strip.title: details on the tools
bort.sum.title: Load by role
bort.sum.weight: tokens per step: weight of all arsenals
bort.sum.legend: length — weight of the node’s arsenal; “−N” — how much of it is wasted
bort.sum.inherit: without a tools field (inherit the session): {list}

st.title: Structure
iv.grow: Expand this item in the interview
iv.asked: Questions of this pass: {got} of {asked} answered.
iv.dead: the interview page is not responding — the button will bring it up again
iv.notWritten: The questions of this pass are not written yet — they are composed together with the human when the position’s turn comes.
iv.err.popup: The browser did not let the tab open. Interview address: {url}
iv.prompt.empty: The first page prompt is not written yet — it is written along the interview, as answers come.
iv.prompt.foot: Edited after every submission, reconciled with all answers on Finish. Unverified is marked “guess”. File: project/brief/landing-prompt.md.
iv.idea.empty: The document is not written yet — it will appear when there is something to build it from.
iv.idea.foot: Rewritten after every answer review. The record of what was said is separate and does not change: project/brief/interview.md.
iv.tree.title: Subject tree · solid outline — said by the human, dashed — the agent’s guess
iv.tree.empty: There is no tree yet — the first position is not answered.
iv.tree.foot: Goals and epics later grow from this tree in the “Chain” tab. Empty branches are not an error, but what has not been asked about yet.
iv.limit: A guess has exactly two actions: ✓ confirm and ✕ reject. Renaming, dragging or adding a node here is impossible — on purpose: the picture is edited by words in the interview, not by the mouse.
iv.unclear: The unclear is clarified by a question in the interview, not by a click here.
iv.brokenPicture: The picture exists but cannot be read: project/brief/picture.json — {err}. Below is the skeleton, not your answers.
iv.notHeld: The brief interview has not been held yet — project/brief/interview.md is empty. Below is what will be asked; the first two positions can be closed right now.
iv.title: Live picture of the project — the brief interview
iv.refreshTip: The picture is redrawn when a round of answers is submitted, not by a phrase

fm.pluginsErr: Plugins: {reason} (expected a JSON array with id/scope/enabled from claude plugin list --json).
fm.pluginsLead: Plugins are engine-level data (claude plugin list --json), not a node’s: the source has no “plugin → specific node” binding, so there is one list for the whole tab.
fm.userScope: User scope: {n} plugin(s), a personal environment — not listed row by row.
fm.rolesMissing: The engine’s role catalog was not found — nodes were not read.
fm.lead: Node card — model, tier, effort, skills, connectors (MCP); source — the role files of the engine “{title}”. An empty field is marked explicitly, not by silence.
fm.noData: No form data — no engine has an adapter with a role inventory (forma-adapter.cjs, field formaRoles).

law.check.agent-id: call id in the attempt line
law.check.engine-tag: engine at the start of the description
law.check.spend-english: key part of the spend line in English
law.role.intent: Intent — end-image, arrival criterion, task check; the voice before the human
law.role.spec: Spec — slicing into tasks, one qualification per card
law.role.kit: Kit — six kit units, a single return channel
law.role.run: Run — does exactly what was assigned, with the skills given
law.role.core: Core — thresholds, cycle verdict, node diagnosis, trend
law.role.extractor: Extractor — text extraction, no route decisions
law.lawNote: The operative text of the law is English (AGENTS.md), the same for every engine. Section titles and prohibitions are also given in Russian; “§N” links on the board lead here.
law.lawNoteEn: The operative text of the law is English (AGENTS.md), the same for every engine; “§N” links on the board lead here.
law.engineNote: .claude/rules/claude-8.md — what is true only for Claude Code: where the roles are, what the nodes are called, which fields carry spend, hooks, MCP.
law.routesNote: Nine routes. route-0…5 open only on the human’s approval of the five fields. Stages are the keys of the stage line; the reason is the why code (§6).
law.rolesNote: Five nodes and a helper: model, effort, tools, the full role text (.claude/agents/).
law.ondemandNote: Files a node reads only at the right moment (.claude/agents/on-demand/).
law.checksNote: node .claude/scripts/sync-engines.cjs --check — the machine that holds the law: it reports a breach. A rule applies from the date in .forma/living/checks.json; earlier cards are not checked.
law.alsoNote: Also: parity of Claude ↔ Gemini ↔ Codex roles, board epics, cards in done without Core’s closing, engine depersonalization.
law.projectNote: project/config/PROJECT.md — thresholds (attempts {a}, cycle volume {v}), epic routes, external services, language.
law.protocolNote: .forma/manual/ru/03-forma/PROTOCOL.md — the protocol for the human, in Russian.
law.prohib.1: Only the receiving node confirms work, not the doer
law.prohib.2: A gap is named precisely: address and expected value
law.prohib.3: The budget changes only through a stop with a report
law.prohib.4: Every node stops itself at its own threshold
law.prohib.5: Failures stay in JOURNAL.md as they are
law.prohib.6: An example is only a shape; the criterion and spec define the requirements
law.prohib.7: The doer gets a clean card, without the history of its failures
law.prohib.8: GOAL.md does not change until the human confirms the goal
law.prohib.9: The cycle cache carries only the unchanging
law.prohib.10: Returning a task changes at least one of the six kit units
law.prohib.11: A human instruction outside the route is recorded as a change
law.prohib.12: Someone else’s defect goes back along the route, not fixed on the spot
law.prohib.13: A discrepancy is named by address and expected value
law.prohib.14: A second identical diagnosis in a row is a stop
law.prohib.15: Credentials live only in VARS/credentials.md or .env; a card refers to them by name
